finding: The 20 rpm per-model new-account cap measured on 2026-09-09 is gone. 240 simultaneous requests now succeed with zero 429s on every model tested.
why_rechecked: The limit key was new-account-rpm/<vendor>/<model>, an explicitly account-age/spend tier. Account spend has since gone from $0.169 to $17.41, so the tier was worth re-measuring before committing to a 111-minute judging run paced at the old ceiling.

conclusion.note: The staircase was stopped at 240 concurrent rather than pushed further: going higher is load on the provider for no decision value, since 240 already removes the rate limit as the binding constraint.
conclusion.fastest_observed: openai/gpt-5.6-sol served 240 concurrent requests in 6.0 s
conclusion.new_binding_constraint: latency and concurrency, no longer the account rate limit

supersedes: The '20 RPM per model' result in this directory's README, and the throttle comments in the six agentic L1 configs. Those were correct when measured -- the 429 bodies named the limit explicitly -- and are now stale.
what_is_unaffected: The 2026-09-12 Avg@16 runner run was executed under the old 0.3 rps throttle and completed with zero 429s and zero retries. Its results are unaffected; only the time it took was constrained.
